clue.text: Something simple to do in 'Pinocchio', say, when staged

definitions.meaning: a task needing no effort at all, an easy job
a stage version of a children's story is a drama written for youngsters

explanation.surface: Putting on a production of Pinocchio is pitched as an easy task.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half literally: a staged Pinocchio is a play for a child, a CHILD'S PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a very easy task likens it to a game for youngsters.

clue.text: Sweet tea finally polished off by copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the word tea has its final letter finished off, removed

explanation.surface: A cup of tea being drained by a policeman, a copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and the answer are synonyms for endearingly pretty or charming.

clue.text: Altogether fashionable lot at broadcast

parts.note: in means fashionable, in vogue

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of lot at are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trendy crowd all present at a broadcast event.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean counting everything, as a sum or overall.

clue.text: Maybe reel in fish, indefinite number caught

indicators.note: the fish has caught the number, holding it inside itself

parts.note: the dace is a small freshwater fish
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: An angler reeling in a fish, having caught an unknown number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe reel' looks like angling; a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is one example of a lively step routine, hence the 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Adhesive material I stripped from column

indicators.note: the letter I is stripped away, taken out of the column word

parts.note: a pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall

explanation.surface: Someone has peeled sticky material off a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is an adhesive dressing; plaster is also a material spread on walls.

clue.text: An American theatre award presented to male opposite

parts.note: the Tony is the Broadway theatre award

explanation.surface: A man receiving a Broadway award.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning, such as hot for cold, is the term defined.

clue.text: Finish second, then first

parts.note: top means first, the highest place

explanation.surface: A race result: second place, then first.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish and to halt are synonyms for bringing something to an end.

clue.text: Logic behind Throckmorton's capital crime

indicators.note: behind means the logic word comes after the capital letter
the capital, the initial letter, of the name Throckmorton is taken

parts.note: reason means logic, rational thought

explanation.surface: The reasoning behind a capital crime by Throckmorton, the Elizabethan plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital crime' looks like one phrase, but 'capital' picks the initial T. Francis Throckmorton was executed in 1584 for plotting against Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest of crimes, historically punished by death.

clue.text: Fire-raiser confronted is giving nothing away

parts.note: a poker stirs up, raises, a fire in the grate
faced means confronted

explanation.surface: An arsonist confronted by police reveals nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire-raiser' suggests an arsonist; here it is the iron rod for stirring coals.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face, as kept by card players, reveals no thoughts.

clue.text: Foreword for the record, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud and a like-sounding word is entered

parts.note: pro means for, and a log is a record, giving pro-log

explanation.surface: A spoken preface, said for the record.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory section of a book or play is a preface, a synonym.

clue.text: Moon having brownish colour around it

indicators.note: the colour word goes around the word it

parts.note: tan is a light yellowish-brown

explanation.surface: A moon whose surface has a brownish hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn's largest satellite bears this name, an example of a moon.

clue.text: Later, adorn part of ship

parts.note: after means later
to deck is to adorn, as in decking the halls

explanation.surface: An instruction to decorate a section of a vessel later.
explanation.definitionFit: The open deck at a vessel's stern is one section of it.

clue.text: Cricketer, in awful heat, getting runs — 100

indicators.note: awful means the letters of heat are in a dreadful mess

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a ton is slang for a hundred, especially a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman struggling in terrible heat but making a century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns HEAT into ATHE. Mike Atherton captained England's Test side in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Atherton is a former England opening batsman and captain.

clue.text: Type of printer seen over in hardware sale

indicators.note: over means the run of letters is turned over, read the other way
in means the letters sit inside the words hardware sale

explanation.surface: Spotting a printer in a hardware store's sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes RESAL from inside 'hardware sale' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: One kind of printer fuses toner using a beam of amplified light.

clue.text: For all to see, wicked person in farewell show

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the farewell word

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all
a devil is a wicked person

explanation.surface: A villain appears in a farewell performance open to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For all to see' is the British U film certificate, meaning suitable for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety entertainment of songs and comic acts is a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Distinguished each sportsman originally on pitch

indicators.note: on means the earlier letters sit on the pitch word, ahead of it

parts.note: all means each, as in a score of two all

indicators.note: originally means the sportsman word supplies only its first letter

parts.note: tar is pitch, the black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A distinguished sportsman on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a playing field, but it is the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast of leading celebrities is described as made up of famous, distinguished names.

clue.text: Mean to go round with one on lake in the gloaming

indicators.note: the stingy word goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: tight means mean, stingy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A walk round a lake in the evening dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloaming is a Scottish word for dusk, the dim light after sunset.

clue.text: Dye master spy's employed

indicators.note: the spy is employed by the master, taken in inside his letters

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree
an agent is a spy, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A spymaster's agent working with dyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A purplish-red aniline colouring is a dye of this name.

clue.text: Throwing away doughy piece of food left out

indicators.note: out means the left letter is taken out of the food word

parts.note: a dumpling is a ball of dough cooked in stew

explanation.surface: Discarding a stodgy dumpling left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumping and throwing away are synonyms for disposing of unwanted things.

clue.text: Again, reportedly fear disposing of a rebellious knight

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, spelt as it sounds

parts.note: more means again, once more

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of the letter a from the fear word

parts.note: dread means fear

explanation.surface: Renewed fear of an Arthurian rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE as heard gives MOR; 'disposing of a' drops the A from DREAD, giving DRED.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend Mordred rebelled against King Arthur and killed him at Camlann.

clue.text: Greek looking for hard worker

parts.note: after means looking for, seeking, as in being after something

explanation.surface: A Greek man seeking a diligent worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is British slang for hard labour, so one who toils is so named.

clue.text: Golden syrup from tin initially put on flaky cereal

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of tin is used
flaky means crumbly, so the letters of cereal fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: Pouring syrup from a tin over flaked breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaky' turns CEREAL into REACLE. Golden syrup is a pale British syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain golden syrup is also called light molasses syrup, a pale form of this sweetener.

clue.text: First-class spinner opening

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A first-rate slow bowler opening the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned British slang for excellent, splendid.

clue.text: Poor Clare, raised and put in order

indicators.note: poor means in a bad state, so the letters of Clare are disordered

parts.note: up means raised

explanation.surface: A Poor Clare nun lifted and tidied.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are an order of nuns, misdirecting 'Poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy a place is to arrange it neatly, the same as this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Composer from Hanover discovered

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run Hanover discovered

explanation.surface: A composer found in the German city of Hanover.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Group of characters from Bath, pale in resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sorted again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors from Bath, looking pale at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city, which makes 'resort' read as a holiday place.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters of a writing system is a group of written characters.

clue.text: A model upset satirist

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down clue the word is turned upside down

parts.note: to pose is to model

explanation.surface: A model is upset by a satirist's mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop's fables mock human folly through animals, making him a satirist of sorts.

clue.text: Pole, not required, finished early

indicators.note: the word is finished early, so it stops short of its last letter

parts.note: spare means not required, surplus

explanation.surface: A Polish worker no longer needed leaves work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a stout pole such as a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, as used for a ship's mast or boom.

clue.text: Somewhat slow, Republican to enter US city slum area

indicators.note: the Republican letter enters, going in between the city and slum letters

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a ghetto is a poor, crowded slum district

explanation.surface: A Republican politician strolling into a deprived district of a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction means fairly slowly, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: Fight in shed

definitions.meaning: to shed, discard or get rid of

explanation.surface: A brawl inside a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut; it is the verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scuffle and to throw away as useless.

clue.text: Toy not starting — current is needed

indicators.note: not starting means the toy word loses its first letter

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A toy won't start, so electric current is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests electricity; here it is water.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl of water against the main stream is a circular current.

clue.text: Request, daily, a note of Westminster schedule

parts.note: to order is to request
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Requesting a daily memo of parliamentary business.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Commons publishes each day's agenda of business on such a printed sheet; Westminster is where Parliament sits.
